name: Orizn Visa API
description:
> Visa requirements, fees, embassies, transit rules and 26 more data points
> for every passport / destination pair in the world — in 15 languages.


The **Orizn Visa API** returns up to **30 data points** for every one of
**49,750 passport × destination pairs**, in **15 languages**.

## Authentication

Three modes depending on the endpoint:

1. **API key** — `x-api-key` request header (or `?api_key=` query param).
   This is what you use for product code.
2. **Public** — no auth at all. Used by `/stats`, `/score`, `/score/compare`,
   `/live*`, `/register`, `/affiliate/register|track-click|apply-referral`.
   The `/visa/check` endpoint is also keyless when the request comes from
   `visa.orizn.app`, `localhost`, or a Chrome extension origin (for the
   public landing demo and the browser extension).
3. **Session cookie** — `orizn_token` cookie. Dashboard-only endpoints
   (key rotation, Stripe checkout/portal). Not callable through a third-party
   gateway like RapidAPI.

## Quota

Five endpoints count against your monthly quota: `/visa`, `/visa/check`,
`/visa/bulk` and `/visa/group` bill one request per call whatever the
number of pairs they resolve; `/visa/decision` bills one request per
distinct country resolved, and reports the figure in `meta.pairs_charged`.
Everything else (stats, score, live, devices, webhooks, team keys, account,
affiliate) is **free against quota**.

Quotas reset on the 1st of each month, UTC.

## Versioning and deprecation

`/v1/` is stable and stays reachable.

- **Additive changes ship without notice** — new fields, new enum members,
  new endpoints. Parse defensively and ignore what you do not recognise.
- **Breaking changes never land in v1.** A removed or renamed field, a
  narrowed type, a removed endpoint: those ship as `/v2`, and `/v1` keeps
  answering.
- **Six months of notice** before anything in v1 stops working, counted
  from the dated entry in the changelog at
  <https://visa.orizn.app/visa-api/changelog>.
- During that window every affected response carries `Deprecation` and
  `Sunset` headers (RFC 9745 / RFC 8594) and a `Link` header to the
  migration note, so your monitoring sees it before your users do.
- No silent removals, no shortened windows.

One endpoint is currently withdrawn: `/api/v1/visa/changes` returns `503`.
See its description below.

## Data quality

Responses carry `source_url` and `last_verified_at` — the official page a
pair was read from and the date it was last read. **Both are `null` on
pairs that have not been re-sourced yet, and that is most of them**: 56 of
199 passport countries currently have an official source on file. Branch on
the field, never on the count.

A separate `requirement_status: "uncertain"` field appears on the pairs
whose legal regime is unsettled — a country that has left a bloc whose
freedom-of-movement treaty was the legal basis for entry. It never replaces
`requirement`, and the key is absent on every unaffected pair.

## Conventions

- All country codes are ISO 3166-1 alpha-3 (`FRA`, `USA`, `JPN`).
- All timestamps are ISO 8601 with a UTC suffix.
- Responses are JSON / UTF-8.
- CORS open on every public endpoint, OPTIONS preflight implemented.
- `/visa` and `/visa/check` also support `Accept: text/markdown` for a
  human-readable rendering.

## SDKs

- **JavaScript / TypeScript** — `npm install orizn`
- **Python** — `pip install orizn`
- **MCP server** (Claude, Cursor, Codex) — `npx orizn-visa-mcp`
